accepted.s: At which place do the headstreams Bhagirathi and Alaknanda unite before the river acquires the name Ganga?
accepted.x: Bhagirathi and Alaknanda unite at Devprayag. Downstream of this confluence, the river is called the Ganga.
accepted.tq: Directly identify the place associated with a river confluence.
accepted.sec: Ganga tributaries - left vs right bank, sources, westernmost/longest, sequence below Prayagraj  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Ganga drainage system:
1. The Ganga swings southward at the Farakka Barrage.
2. Its left arm at Farakka is the Bhagirathi-Hooghly.
3. Its right arm is the Padma, which flows into Bangladesh.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. At Farakka, the Ganga divides into the Bhagirathi-Hooghly on the left and the Padma on the right, which enters Bangladesh.
accepted.tq: Test the division of a river at a named barrage through a coded statement set.
accepted.sec: Ganga tributaries - left vs right bank, sources, westernmost/longest, sequence below Prayagraj  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Padma, after joining the Brahmaputra and the Meghna, enters the Bay of Bengal as the
accepted.x: The Padma joins the Brahmaputra and Meghna system and enters the Bay of Bengal as the Meghna.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the successive names of a transboundary river system.
accepted.sec: Ganga tributaries - left vs right bank, sources, westernmost/longest, sequence below Prayagraj  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The total length of the Ganga is approximately
accepted.x: The commonly cited total length of the Ganga is about 2,525 km. The figures 2,465 km and 2,071 km represent alternative figures given for the total and Indian stretches in some compilations.
accepted.tq: Distinguish closely related length figures by identifying the standard total value.
accepted.sec: Ganga tributaries - left vs right bank, sources, westernmost/longest, sequence below Prayagraj  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements about the Ganga basin is correct?
o: It covers about 9,51,600 square kilometres and drains less than 5 per cent of India’s area.
It covers about 2,525 square kilometres and drains nearly 40 per cent of India’s area.
It covers about 2,071 square kilometres and drains nearly 9 per cent of India’s area.
It covers about 9,51,600 square kilometres and drains nearly 40 per cent of India’s area.
accepted.x: The Ganga basin is approximately 9,51,600 sq km in total and drains nearly 40 per cent of India’s area.
accepted.tq: Match a basin-area figure with its corresponding share of national drainage.
accepted.sec: Ganga tributaries - left vs right bank, sources, westernmost/longest, sequence below Prayagraj  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Ganga is navigable up to which of the following places?
accepted.x: The Ganga is navigable up to Prayagraj.
accepted.tq: Recall the specified navigable limit of a river.
accepted.sec: Ganga tributaries - left vs right bank, sources, westernmost/longest, sequence below Prayagraj  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with the bank of the Ganga on which it is classified as a tributary?
accepted.x: Damodar is a right-bank tributary of the Ganga. Gomti, Kosi and other listed Himalayan tributaries are left-bank tributaries, while Son is a right-bank tributary.
accepted.tq: Use bank-side classification to separate geographically close tributaries.
accepted.sec: Ganga tributaries - left vs right bank, sources, westernmost/longest, sequence below Prayagraj  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Son — joins the Ganga near Maner
Yamuna — joins the Ganga at Prayagraj
Ramganga — joins the Ganga near Farrukhabad
accepted.x: The Gandak enters India at Valmikinagar, not Raxaul. Ramganga joins near Farrukhabad, Yamuna at Prayagraj and Son near Maner.
accepted.tq: Find the wrong location attached to a tributary.
accepted.sec: Ganga tributaries - left vs right bank, sources, westernmost/longest, sequence below Prayagraj  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Son is regarded as the second-largest right-bank tributary of the Ganga after the Yamuna. It joins the Ganga near
accepted.x: The Son is the second-largest right-bank tributary after the Yamuna and joins the Ganga near Maner, close to Patna.
accepted.tq: Combine rank and confluence location to identify a tributary.
accepted.sec: Ganga tributaries - left vs right bank, sources, westernmost/longest, sequence below Prayagraj  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Gandak is known as which of the following names in Nepal?
accepted.x: The Gandak is known as Narayani in Nepal. Sadanira is its name in the Shatapatha Brahmana.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between regional and historical names of the same river.
accepted.sec: Ganga tributaries - left vs right bank, sources, westernmost/longest, sequence below Prayagraj  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which historical text refers to the Gandak as ‘Sadanira’?
accepted.x: The Gandak is referred to as Sadanira in the Shatapatha Brahmana.
accepted.tq: Link an ancient textual name with the river to which it refers.
accepted.sec: Ganga tributaries - left vs right bank, sources, westernmost/longest, sequence below Prayagraj  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched with a tributary of the Yamuna and its source?
accepted.x: The Chambal originates near Mhow in Madhya Pradesh. Betwa, Ken and Hindon have different source regions from those stated in the other options.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure river-source pair and eliminate swapped origins.
accepted.sec: Ganga tributaries - left vs right bank, sources, westernmost/longest, sequence below Prayagraj  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following rivers is a left-bank tributary of the Yamuna?
accepted.x: Hindon is a left-bank tributary of the Yamuna. Chambal, Betwa and Ken are right-bank tributaries.
accepted.tq: Apply the left-bank/right-bank distinction to a tributary system.
accepted.sec: Ganga tributaries - left vs right bank, sources, westernmost/longest, sequence below Prayagraj  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following tributaries of the Ganga in their west-to-east order of confluence below Prayagraj:
A. Gandak
B. Son
C. Kosi
D. Ghaghara
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The relevant sequence is Ghaghara, Son, Gandak and Kosi from west to east. Therefore, the order is D, B, A, C.
accepted.tq: Use the west-to-east sequence and fix the first two confluences before checking the rest.
accepted.sec: Ganga tributaries - left vs right bank, sources, westernmost/longest, sequence below Prayagraj  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Indus originates at Singge Khabab at an elevation of approximately
accepted.x: The Indus rises at Singge Khabab in the Kailash range at approximately 5,182 metres.
accepted.tq: Recall the distinctive elevation associated with the river’s source.
accepted.sec: Indus system - tributaries west to east, largest tributary, Greek names, IWT  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Indus flows westward between which two mountain ranges before turning south near Nanga Parbat?
accepted.x: The Indus flows west between the Ladakh and Zaskar ranges and turns south near Nanga Parbat.
accepted.tq: Identify the paired mountain ranges associated with a river course.
accepted.sec: Indus system - tributaries west to east, largest tributary, Greek names, IWT  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The turn of the Indus near Nanga Parbat is associated with its passage through
accepted.x: Near Nanga Parbat, the Indus turns south through an antecedent gorge before flowing towards the Arabian Sea.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the geomorphic feature associated with a river’s course.
accepted.sec: Indus system - tributaries west to east, largest tributary, Greek names, IWT  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
accepted.x: Ravi was known to the Greeks as Hydraotes. Hyphasis is the Greek name of the Beas.
accepted.tq: Use the Greek-name table to detect a swapped river name.
accepted.sec: Indus system - tributaries west to east, largest tributary, Greek names, IWT  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Chenab is formed by the confluence of which two rivers at Tandi in Himachal Pradesh?
accepted.x: The Chenab is formed by the union of the Chandra and Bhaga rivers at Tandi in Himachal Pradesh.
accepted.tq: Identify the constituent streams of a major river.
accepted.sec: Indus system - tributaries west to east, largest tributary, Greek names, IWT  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Salal, identified as India’s first project in the region under the Indus Waters Treaty, is a hydropower project on the
accepted.x: The Salal project is a 690 MW NHPC project on the Chenab and is identified as India’s first project in the region under the treaty.
accepted.tq: Match a project with the river on which it is situated.
accepted.sec: Indus system - tributaries west to east, largest tributary, Greek names, IWT  [APPSC]

accepted.s: According to the cited IIT-Gandhinagar study for 1980–2021, the flow of the Indus increased by approximately
accepted.x: The study reported an approximately 8 per cent increase in Indus flows, while Ganga flows declined by about 17 per cent during the period.
accepted.tq: Separate the increase figure from the contrasting decline figure in a paired statistic.
accepted.sec: Indus system - tributaries west to east, largest tributary, Greek names, IWT  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Brahmaputra rises at which glacier in the Kailash range?
accepted.x: The Brahmaputra rises at the Chemayungdung Glacier in the Kailash range, east of Lake Mansarovar.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the source glacier of one Himalayan river from those of other major rivers.
accepted.sec: Brahmaputra - names across countries, Majuli, tributaries  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements regarding the Brahmaputra is correct?
1. It is about 2,900 km long.
2. Only about 885 km of its course lies in India.
3. It is ranked ninth in the world by volume.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: All three statements are correct: the Brahmaputra is about 2,900 km long, has an approximately 885 km course in India, and ranks ninth globally by volume.
accepted.tq: Combine length, national-stretch and world-rank figures in a coded question.
accepted.sec: Brahmaputra - names across countries, Majuli, tributaries  [APPSC]

accepted.s: At which place does the Brahmaputra turn southward after flowing through Tibet?
accepted.x: The river, known as the Tsangpo or Yarlung Zangbo in Tibet, turns south at Namche Barwa.
accepted.tq: Associate a major change in river direction with its landmark location.
accepted.sec: Brahmaputra - names across countries, Majuli, tributaries  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which sequence correctly represents the names of the Brahmaputra from Arunachal Pradesh to Bangladesh?
accepted.x: In Arunachal Pradesh it is called Dihang or Siang, in Assam Brahmaputra, and in Bangladesh Jamuna.
accepted.tq: Arrange successive regional names along the downstream course.
accepted.sec: Brahmaputra - names across countries, Majuli, tributaries  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Dihang becomes the Brahmaputra in Assam after the confluence of which rivers near Pasighat/Sadiya?
accepted.x: Dibang and Lohit join the Dihang near Pasighat/Sadiya, after which the combined river is called the Brahmaputra.
accepted.tq: Identify the tributaries responsible for a change in the river’s regional name.
accepted.sec: Brahmaputra - names across countries, Majuli, tributaries  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is a right-bank tributary of the Brahmaputra?
accepted.x: Subansiri is a northern, Himalayan or right-bank tributary of the Brahmaputra. Burhi Dihing, Dhansiri and Dikhu are southern or left-bank tributaries.
accepted.tq: Apply the river-bank convention to distinguish northern and southern tributaries.
accepted.sec: Brahmaputra - names across countries, Majuli, its tributaries  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the Teesta:
1. It is approximately 414 km long.
2. It rises at Tso Lhamo Lake in North Sikkim.
3. Rangeet is its largest tributary.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The Teesta is about 414 km long, rises at Tso Lhamo Lake and has the Rangeet as its largest tributary.
accepted.tq: Test a river through a combination of length, source and largest-tributary facts.
accepted.sec: Brahmaputra - names across countries, Majuli, its tributaries  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The draft treaty concerning the sharing of the Teesta waters remains
o: replaced by the Indus Waters Treaty
accepted.x: The draft 2011 treaty on Teesta water sharing remains stalled.
accepted.tq: Identify the status of an inter-country water-sharing arrangement without confusing it with another treaty.
accepted.sec: Brahmaputra - names across countries, Majuli, its tributaries  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly states the dimensions of Majuli given in the geographical description?
accepted.x: Majuli is described as approximately 60 km long and 20 km wide.
accepted.tq: Test a distinctive paired-size figure rather than the island’s commonly repeated identity.
accepted.sec: Brahmaputra - names across countries, Majuli, its tributaries  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Brahmaputra is popularly known as the ‘Sorrow of’
accepted.x: The Brahmaputra is known as the ‘Sorrow of Assam’.
accepted.tq: Match a river sobriquet with the correct region.
accepted.sec: Brahmaputra - names across countries, Majuli, its tributaries  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Brahmaputra is navigable for approximately how far up to Dibrugarh?
accepted.x: The Brahmaputra is navigable for approximately 1,280 km up to Dibrugarh.
accepted.tq: Distinguish navigable length from total river length and Indian course length.
accepted.sec: Brahmaputra - names across countries, Majuli, its tributaries  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
accepted.x: The Indus originates at Singge Khabab. Sutlej rises near Rakas Tal, Brahmaputra at Chemayungdung Glacier, and Karnali in the Mansarovar-Kailash area rather than at the locations stated.
accepted.tq: Match rivers with source locations while rejecting familiar but swapped Himalayan origins.
accepted.sec: Rivers originating near Mansarovar - which do and which do not  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following rivers originates in the Mansarovar–Kailash area but does not rise directly from Gangotri or Yamunotri?
accepted.x: The Sutlej originates in the Mansarovar–Kailash region, near Rakas Tal. The Ganga rises at Gangotri, Yamuna at Yamunotri and Jhelum at Verinag.
accepted.tq: Separate rivers of the Mansarovar–Kailash group from those of the Himalayan source group.
accepted.sec: Rivers originating near Mansarovar - which do and which do not  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following rivers does NOT originate in the Mansarovar–Kailash area?
accepted.x: The Beas originates near the Rohtang region, not in the Mansarovar–Kailash area. Karnali, Indus and Brahmaputra are included among the rivers originating in or near that region.
accepted.tq: Find the outsider in a grouped source-location list.
accepted.sec: Rivers originating near Mansarovar - which do and which do not  [APPSC]
